title: WARDEN — private browser
shortDescription: Privacy-first browsing for admins: no account, no telemetry, no sensors.
fullDescription:
WARDEN is a privacy-first browser and operator console for security and network administrators.

This mobile build is the secure entry point: it opens pages in the system browser (Chrome Custom Tabs), stores nothing of its own about what you read, ships no analytics, crash or advertising SDKs, and tells you what the session's posture actually is instead of showing a green shield and hoping.

WHAT IT DOES
• Nothing stored: no browsing history, no profile, no identifiers and no account — the app keeps only its own preferences.
• System browser: pages open in Chrome Custom Tabs, which the app cannot read or script, so a page never shares a session with the app's interface.
• No telemetry: no analytics SDK, no crash reporter, no tracking identifiers, no ad SDKs.
• No sensor access: the app never requests camera or microphone.
• 38 KB of UI, no bundled trackers, no in-app purchases.

The desktop WARDEN (Windows) adds request-level ad and tracker blocking, a PTY shell, mail, messaging and site deconstruction. The mobile app is the companion entry point while the embedded engine lands; the plan is public in the repository.

WHO IT IS FOR
Security administrators and network administrators who want a browser that refuses by default and explains its refusals. No account required, no configuration to start.

PRIVACY POLICY
https://innotelinc.github.io/warden/privacy.html

contentRating.questionnaire: No user-generated content, no ads, no purchases, no location, no camera or microphone. Rate: Everyone.

dataSafety.deletionRequest: No data is collected, so there is nothing to delete; uninstalling removes the app's local preferences.
dataSafety.notes: The app has no analytics or crash SDK. Pages opened in the platform browser surface are governed by that browser's own policy and by the sites themselves.

notes: Upload the signed .aab produced by .github/workflows/mobile-android.yml. First release also needs the Play Console data-safety form filled from dataSafety above and the content-rating questionnaire answered as described.
